requirement:
Each `AgentConfig` variant carries the corresponding settings from
`trust_but_verify::agent`. Serde uses the `backend` field to select `bedrock`,
`openai`, or `ollama` and reads the settings from the same object.

Choose [`BedrockConfig`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.BedrockConfig),
[`OpenAiConfig`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OpenAiConfig), or
[`OllamaConfig`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OllamaConfig) for the selected backend.
With settings omitted, OpenAI uses `gpt-6.1-sol`, `https://api.openai.com/v1`,
and `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Ollama defaults to `http://localhost:11434`.

All three backend constructors start with an empty `options` map. Calling
`option(key, value)` inserts one inference setting. Calling it again with the
same key replaces its value and preserves the other settings. An `OptionValue` is
a `String`, `Boolean`, `Integer(i64)`, `Float(f64)`, `Array`, or `Map`. Arrays hold
option values and maps associate strings with option values. These serialize as
the corresponding untagged values. Backend calls reject nonfinite floats,
including those nested in an array or map.

`BedrockCredentials` contains `access_key_id` and `secret_access_key`, both
`SecretString`, and an optional `session_token` of the same type. Construct a
`SecretString` from `String` or `&str`. `expose_secret()` borrows its value.
Serialization preserves the string, while `Debug` prints `<redacted>`.
rationale:
## Verdict
The marked tests cover most of `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.agent_config.settings`. One stated default has no test: the OpenAI default credential variable `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

## Obligations and coverage

- **Serde `backend` field selects the variant and the settings share one object.**
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/config.rs#mod[tests]/fn[all_backends_preserve_nested_settings_and_credentials]` deserializes `bedrock`, `openai` and `ollama` objects into `AgentConfig`.
  - It asserts the serialized value equals the input, and that a JSON string round trip is equal.
  - `fn[configuration_debug_hides_credentials]` asserts that an unknown field is rejected.
- **Constructors start with an empty `options` map.** `fn[backend_builders_set_only_the_requested_fields]` asserts that the serialized new configs contain only the model, with no `options` key, for all three backends.
- **`option(key, value)` inserts one setting, and the same key replaces its value while other settings are preserved.** This is tested on `BedrockConfig` only, by setting `a` to 1, `b` to true, then `a` to 2, and asserting `{"a":2,"b":true}`. The OpenAI and Ollama `option` methods have the same one-line body, so this is not treated as a gap.
- **`OptionValue` variants and untagged serialization.**
  - The round-trip test covers integer, float, string, boolean, array and nested map values.
  - `fn[option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic]` asserts that `json!(1)` deserializes to `Integer(1)` and `json!(1.0)` to `Float(1.0)`.
- **Backend calls reject nonfinite floats, including nested ones.** In the same test, `OptionValue::Map` containing `INFINITY` fails `validate()`. An Ollama `options_json()` call with an array containing `NaN` returns an error.
- **OpenAI defaults when settings are omitted.** `OpenAiConfig::default()` resolves to model `gpt-6.1-sol` and endpoint `https://api.openai.com/v1`. Both are asserted.
- **Ollama default endpoint.** `OllamaConfig::new(..).resolved_endpoint()` is asserted to be `http://localhost:11434`.
- **`BedrockCredentials`.**
  - Required fields and the optional `session_token` are asserted by JSON comparison.
  - Round-trip equality is asserted.
  - A configuration with a token is asserted to differ from one without.
- **`SecretString`.**
  - It is built from `&str` and `String`.
  - `expose_secret()` is asserted to return the value.
  - `Debug` is asserted to print `<redacted>`.
  - Serialization preserves the string.

## Gap
The requirement says that with settings omitted, OpenAI uses `OPENAI_API_KEY`. In `impl[OpenAiConfig]#2/fn[resolved_api_key]`, this default is the `unwrap_or("OPENAI_API_KEY")` branch taken when `api_key_env` is `None`.

The tests never check this branch:
- The OpenAI resolution assertions all set `api_key_env` to `TBV_TEST_ABSENT_BACKEND_KEY` or set `api_key`.
- The `credential(...)` assertions use a caller-supplied name, `MISSING`, `EMPTY` or `PRESENT`, and never the OpenAI default.
- `resolved_api_key` reads `std::env::var_os` directly, so no existing test covers this branch.

An implementation that defaulted to another variable, such as `OPENAI_KEY`, or to none, would pass every marked test.

The testing exemption for environment variables does not apply. The project already has a subprocess-with-controlled-environment pattern in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[explicit_bedrock_credentials_reach_the_sdk_without_the_default_chain]`. That pattern could be used here. The default is also a conditional choice, not a pass-through.

## Conclusion
All other obligations have tests with relevant assertions. The missing test for the default `OPENAI_API_KEY` is an unacknowledged gap, and there are no `{fixme}` acknowledgments.
